title: Review: Total internal reflection and optical fibers; Lenses; Progressive waves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W13-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W13-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W01-1#N.15, W05-1#N.3b, W13-1#N.10, W01-1#N.13, W05-1#N.5b, W13-1#N.9, W01-1#N.1, W13-1#N.8a, W01-1#N.4. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position.

items.label: Focal length
items.clue: Distance from the middle of a thin lens to F, the same on each side.

items.label: Virtual image
items.clue: Formed where rays only appear to come from, so no screen can show it.

items.label: Longitudinal wave
items.clue: Has oscillations parallel to the direction of energy transfer, as in sound.

questions.stem: A vibrator sends waves along a stretched string at constant tension. At 25 Hz the wavelength is 0.80 m. The frequency is raised to 100 Hz. What is the new wavelength, and how long does a wave now take to travel 4.0 m along the string?

options.text: 0.20 m, and it takes 0.050 s
0.80 m, and it takes 0.050 s
0.20 m, and it takes 0.20 s
3.2 m, and it takes 0.20 s

questions.explanation: v = fλ = 25 × 0.80 = 20 m s⁻¹, unchanged. New λ = 20/100 = 0.20 m; time = 4.0/20 = 0.20 s, the same as before.

questions.stem: Light can cross a flat boundary between water (n = 1.33) and glass (n = 1.50) in either direction. Which statement about total internal reflection at this boundary is correct?

options.text: It can occur for light in the glass heading toward the water.
It can occur for light that is in the water and heading toward the glass.
It can occur for light going either way, if the angle is large enough.
It needs air beyond the boundary, so it does not occur at this one.

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light heading into a lower refractive index: here, light in the glass (1.50) meeting the water (1.33), at angles of incidence above sin⁻¹(1.33/1.50), about 62°.

questions.stem: A projector has a thin converging lens of focal length 8.0 cm. A slide is placed 9.0 cm from the lens, close to it. Which describes the image?

options.text: Virtual, upright, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, smaller, 4.2 cm from the lens
Real, upright, 8 times larger, 72 cm from the lens

questions.explanation: The slide is outside F, so the rays really meet: real and inverted. Image distance: 1/(1/8.0 − 1/9.0) = 72 cm; magnification 72/9.0 = 8. That is why a projector's slide goes in upside down.

questions.stem: A pulse travels at 5.00 m/s along a taut rope. The rope is replaced by a second rope that has the same total mass but twice the length, and the tension is doubled. What is the speed of a pulse on the second rope?

For light inside a block of glass striking a glass–air boundary, the critical angle is 41.8°. The block is then placed in water (n = 1.33). What is the critical angle for light inside the glass striking the glass–water boundary? Take n_air = 1.00.
An object 3.0 cm tall is placed 30.0 cm from a thin converging lens of focal length 20.0 cm. What is the height of the image?

options.text: 1.5 cm
6.0 cm
1.2 cm
2.0 cm

questions.stem: A loudspeaker plays a steady note to a listener 5 m away in a room with still air. Which of the following travels from the loudspeaker to the listener?

options.text: Energy, passed along by air molecules that vibrate about fixed positions
Air molecules, pushed across the room from the loudspeaker to the ear
Sound particles, which the loudspeaker gives off and the air carries
An electromagnetic signal, which needs no air to carry it across

questions.stem: An object is placed 24.0 cm from a thin diverging lens whose focal length has a magnitude of 12.0 cm. Use the convention that s_o is positive, s_i is positive for an image on the side of the lens opposite the object and negative for an image on the same side as the object, and f is positive for a converging lens and negative for a diverging lens. What is the image distance s_i?

An electric bell rings inside a sealed glass jar and can be both seen and heard. A pump gradually removes the air from the jar while the bell keeps working. Which prediction, with its explanation, is correct?

options.text: The sound fades and the bell vanishes from view, since both waves need air to travel.
Neither changes, because sound, like light, can travel through an evacuated jar.
The sound fades but the bell stays visible: light, unlike sound, needs no medium.
The sound fades but the bell stays visible, since only longitudinal waves need a medium.
